acceptance_criteria.criterion: filterText() trims whitespace, strips newlines, and returns '' for purely numeric strings
filterText() preserves strings like 'Chapter 1' unchanged after trimming
autoPopulateFromEpisodes() populates chapter, title, and altText for entries that lack them, reading from existing info.json files
autoPopulateFromEpisodes() does not overwrite entries that already have non-empty values for those keys
No HTTP requests or file writes occur during auto-population (read-only on existing local files)
Methods are private and not part of the public interface

summary: filterText() implemented as private method: trims whitespace, strips CR/LF, blanks numeric-only strings. autoPopulateFromEpisodes() iterates indexEntries, skips entries where all metadata keys are already populated, instantiates Episode for each remaining entry, reads info.json via parse(), applies filterText(), and only writes non-empty values. Both methods are private. No HTTP requests or writes during auto-population.

All 6 AC verified. filterText() and autoPopulateFromEpisodes() tested via 14 targeted tests (all pass) in base suite of 28/28. No HTTP calls or file writes occur during auto-population confirmed by code inspection. Both methods declared private. Zero regressions.

metrics.test_coverage: AC1-AC6 fully covered by tests 5-14 (filterText data provider, autoPopulate 3 scenarios)

summary: Code review passed. filterText() is a clean, correctly-ordered string utility. autoPopulateFromEpisodes() has a well-placed needsPopulation guard that avoids all I/O when not needed, uses raw info.json parsing (correctly avoiding getter fallbacks), and follows the same reference-loop + unset pattern established in WP-001. Two non-blocking suggestions recorded."

comments.note: The $metadataKeys array in autoPopulateFromEpisodes is a hardcoded local array. This is the single place to update when new metadata keys are introduced; worth adding an inline comment documenting this intent to avoid future maintainers missing it.

autoPopulateFromEpisodes instantiates Episode with position=0 solely for file-path resolution. A brief inline comment like '// position 0 — only used for file path resolution, not display order' would clarify why 0 is passed to future maintainers.

The needsPopulation early-exit guard in autoPopulateFromEpisodes correctly separates the 'do we need to read from disk at all?' decision from the per-key merge logic, keeping file I/O cost at zero for fully-populated entries.

summary: Added two inline comments to autoPopulateFromEpisodes() per code-review suggestions: (1) on $metadataKeys explaining it is the single canonical list to update when extending the index schema; (2) on new Episode(..., 0) clarifying that position 0 is used for file-path resolution only, not display order. filterText() PHPDoc block already present. 28/28 tests pass.
